title: Bosch GDS 18V-1000 18V Li-ion Cordless 1/2" High Torque Impact Wrench - Skin Only $315 (RRP $596) + Bosch Redemption @ Syd Tools
body:
Deal: Bosch GDS 18V-1000 18V Li-ion Cordless 1/2" High Torque Impact Wrench - Skin Only $315 (RRP $596) + Bosch Redemption @ Syd Tools

[BrownManWalking] Been waiting for my redemption since early June. They said it'll be processed in August.. Buyer beware
[schquid] Took about 10 for my last one. I think the 8 week mark is when they consider getting it off the shelf, and 9 is when they ponder shipping it.
Dunno why it's such a lengthy process with them. The other brands I've had redemptions with turned it around in 1-2 weeks.
[jimojr] I’ve received one battery pack so far, but it was a 4Ah battery instead of the 5Ah one. I redeemed it on 22/06 and I’m still waiting for the other two to arrive.
[jimojr] If you buy it together with this kit , you can also qualify for an extra battery or grinder.
[fatduckling] Does that mean if I buy this alone, I won't get the free battery or grinder?
[jimojr] You can only get the free battery and charger when you buy this alone. If you spend $449 or more, you can also get an extra battery, grinder, or laser distance measurer. I’d definitely choose the grinder because it offers more value. If you prefer the battery, you can always sell it and use the money to get three batteries instead.
[yaaNaa] Says redemtion if spend is 449 at least, this seems not eligble, am i mistaken?
[JURBA] Wish this came with the A and B preset buttons like on the Bosch GDS 18V-1000c. The A Includes dedicated Metal (A) and Wood (B) modes to prevent snapped screw heads or lost nuts by automatically slowing down or shutting off.
[JURBA] the Bosch GDS 18V-1600 HC is 60% more powerfull and comes with AB button but have to pay extra $64. better purchase in my opinion. rather not loose nuts or break screw heads etc
[JURBA] but i guess it depends what your using it for and if you already have 1/2" or 3/4" impact sockets etc. and the size of the nuts bolts your tackling etc
[fatduckling] Also the 3/4 sockets are lot more expensive. I already have the sockets + breaker bar + torque wrench etc in 1/2 size. If I upgrade to the 3/4 impact wrench, I have to change everything around. Otherwise I could get an 3/4 to 1/2 adapter? Thoughts?
[JURBA] yeah thats what i was just looking at, the adaptor because those 3/4 sockets are like $400+ on average. that way you have the flexibility to go big in the future if you have to
[fatduckling] We can get the Milwaukee one? https://sydneytools.com.au/product/milwaukee-49666728-shockw…
[JURBA] question is what could i buy from total tools for extra $70 to meet redemption minimum?
or would buying from totalkitdepot and getting the following be better?
BONUS GEAR VIA REDEMPTION
BONUS Bosch 18V 5.0ah Starter Set - 0615990M1Z
Offer Valid 1/07/26 - 30/09/26?
[fatduckling] What's the difference with toolkitdepot? They have the 3/4 impact wrench the same price ($379) so you still need $70 to hit the minimum.
I was thinking of getting the right angle impact wrench as well. The 1/2 inch one. https://sydneytools.com.au/product/bosch-grc-12v60-12-sn-pro…
[JURBA] @fatduckling: i just foundout
" The "Starter Set" bonus is triggered by the specific model number (06019M1000) of the tool you are buying, not by a dollar spend threshold."
"Stacking Rules: Bosch promotions generally do not allow stacking. You typically get one redemption per eligible tool. Since your tool already qualifies for the 5.0Ah Starter Set (valued at ~$150-$200), adding extra fillers to reach $449 would likely not unlock a second bonus on the same invoice, nor would it upgrade your current bonus to a higher tier (unless you bought a completely different "Tier 2" tool).Verdict: Save the ~$70 difference. The $379 price at Tool Kit Depot is sufficient to claim the battery and charger set."
so with only buying the specific impact wrench for $379, when you redeem you should have redemption choice between 18V Orbital Sander or 18V 5.0Ah Starter Kit.
https://www.boschbluecrew.com.au/Promotions/Content/Docs/Q3-…
[fatduckling] @JURBA: Thank you for this. So here's what I'm thinking. My friend and I want the same impact wrench.
So we will buy the following in 1 transaction:
* Impact wrench 1: $379 (receive free 18v starter set)
* Impact wrench 2: $379 (receive another free 18v starter set)
* Right angled impact wrench: $249 (receive 12v starter set)
* Total cost of everything: $1007 (eligible for 'Spend $749 in one transaction' - receive 2x 18v batteries?)
I'm assuming I won't be eligible for 'spend $749 in one transaction' because I already claimed the impact individually right?
[JURBA] @fatduckling: In the T&Cs and the plan won't work. Point 8 says you only get one claim per receipt, no matter how many eligible products are on it. So all three tools on the one invoice gets you one gift, not three.
At $1007 you'd be claiming the $749 tier, which is the GBH 18V-22 rotary hammer plus a 5.0Ah battery, around $608 worth. The other two tools wouldn't earn you anything.
You're better off doing three separate transactions:
Wrench 1 ($379) = 18V 5.0Ah starter set, $269
Wrench 2 ($379) on your mate's own receipt = another starter set, $269
Right angle wrench ($249) = 12V 2.0Ah starter set, $145
That's $683 worth for the same money. You just need to submit each claim separately. There's a cap of five claims per person for the quarter, so three is fine.
Also ignore what I said earlier about the sander, I was wrong. The sander comes from spending $299 on Expert accessories and it's Sydney Tools only. The wrench redemption is just the 5.0Ah starter set, there's no choice.
This $379 impact wrench could be abit risky though, because clause 6a, says it excludes clearance and specially discounted stock, and Bosch decides what counts. A $379 price might get questioned. But im just guessing it should be fine. Because they put the add on the page of toolkitdepot that you can get the redemption item and its on their list of tools that qualify for redemption.
https://www.boschbluecrew.com.au/GearUp2026/Content/Docs/Bos…
[fatduckling] @JURBA: Thank you again so much. I'll claim them as individual transactions and try my luck. Cheers
[JURBA] @fatduckling: hey mate for the tool its recommended to use the ProCORE18V battery 5.5Ah, 8.0Ah, or 12.0Ah batteries. the one in the kit isnt procore, so you might be able to use the wrench on its lowest settings. but if you dont have procore you'll probably need to get some. can get cheap on ebay have a look before buying if you havent got any yet.
[fatduckling] @JURBA: I see, yeah the ProCORE batteries are expensive. In that case, the 1/2" ($315) should be fine for now I think. I can then just use the standard starter battery that comes with it right? The 3/4 then might be overkill if I have to buy the adapter/reducer and the ProCORE batteries and eventually 3/4 sockets in the future if any deals come up.
[JURBA] @fatduckling: yeah the Bosch GDS 18V-1000 would run better on the standard batteries than the Bosch GDS 18V-1600 HC for sure. 1600 HC is overkill ay. probably never endup having a need to use the extra power from the 1600 HC in random around the house DIY stuff. its for heavy machinery/heavy steel construction use they say etc. but its upto you. no pressure, buy or dont buy what is best for you. if you need it might not even be worth buying. im just telling myself one day it'll come in handy hahaha i dont need this for my job. but i do some apprenticeship carpentry back in the day and i'll never forget the day we were trying to take out a big bolt from the metal post and it wouldnt budge haha. if i had one of these it would have been easy hehe. goodluck to you my friend
[fatduckling] @JURBA: Thank you again. I'm trying to learn to change parts under a new classic Land Rover Defender I bought so I'm researching into whether 1600 HC is an overkill or whether I can get away with the standard GDS 18V-1000. I don't suppose you have any experience here?
[JURBA] @fatduckling: no sorry i dont mate but what ive read is "Three torque stages at 350 / 650 / 1000 Nm, so you can dial it down."
"Defender wheel nuts are around 130 Nm. Even heavy suspension and chassis bolts are typically 200–250 Nm. Stage 1 alone covers most of what you'll touch."
[fatduckling] @JURBA: Hi @JURBA I decided to just stick to the 1/2" wrench. A lot of comments online suggest 1/2" is plenty. Thank you.
[fatduckling] @JURBA: The procore 8ah batteries are like $100-200 on eBay. Would they be legit? eg https://www.ebay.com.au/itm/178400698193 or https://www.ebay.com.au/itm/137611994539
[JURBA] @fatduckling: i got all my bosch 8ah from ebay for around $147 in january 2024 and they worked good ever since, brand new etc. but idk if can register for warranty only think its abit of a risk. just make sure its not a replacement battery, alott of fake batteries on ebay, will say "replacement for…" etc. triple check and also check the seller reviews is what i do personally. easy to get scammed with batteries on ebay, be super careful
[JURBA] @fatduckling: the tool might even shut off after a few seconds if you dont use the recommended battery because these biturbo tools have higher battery drain than the non-bi turbo
[JURBA] @fatduckling: but beware if your planning to use those batteries on that wrench.. The tool has a massive BITURBO motor that demands a ton of power. The standard 5.0Ah battery can't feed it fast enough. If he tries to blast a really tight bolt, the battery will overheat and shut itself off after 2 seconds to protect itself possibly.To actually get the 1,600 Nm of power you need to use ProCORE18V battery (5.5Ah, 8.0Ah, or 12.0Ah).
